summary: A convenient daytime food stop beside Chatuchak, with carefully displayed fruit, regional ingredients and prepared Thai meals. Choose it for tasting and lunch rather than bargain shopping: the tourism authority describes premium produce and correspondingly higher prices. It also works on weekdays when the main Chatuchak weekend market is not running.
whyGo: Compare Thai fruit, herbs, rice, dried goods and ready-to-eat dishes in one covered market.
Eat at the food court or buy a takeaway picnic before continuing around Chatuchak.
An easy MRT connection makes this a practical independent food outing.
bestFor: A relaxed lunch alongside Chatuchak shopping
skipIf: Your priority is the cheapest produce in Bangkok.
You want evening entertainment or a night market.
duration: Allow 60–90 minutes for browsing and a meal; this is a planning estimate, excluding Chatuchak.
cost: No admission charge is reported. Budget roughly THB 150–350 per person for a meal, drink and modest tasting purchases; this is a planning estimate, not a stall tariff. Premium fruit, especially durian, can cost considerably more. Ask the price and portion weight before buying.
hours: Daytime daily. Published tourism sources conflict: the Korean TAT guide lists 06:00–18:00, while TAT Japan says approximately 06:00–20:00. Plan a morning or lunch visit and reconfirm if relying on early or late hours.
bestTime: Around 09:00–11:00 is a sensible planning window for browsing before lunch and the hottest part of the day. Individual vendors may keep different hours.
gettingThere: Take the MRT Blue Line to Kamphaeng Phet and use exit 3, as listed in the TAT Korean guide. The market is across the road from Chatuchak Weekend Market, at 101 Kamphaeng Phet Road. MRT is more direct than arriving at BTS Mo Chit and walking.
booking: Independent browsing needs no advance booking; buy food directly from vendors.
accessibility: The tourism authority describes a spacious covered building, but a verified step-free route, accessible toilets and stall-level access were not established. Travellers who require these facilities should confirm before visiting.
practicalTips: Bring small cash notes; do not assume foreign cards or Thai QR payment will work for you.
Buy ripe fruit for eating that day and check any restrictions before carrying food onward.
Confirm ingredients directly if you have allergies or dietary requirements.
decemberNotes: Suitable as a daytime December 2026 stop, preferably paired with Chatuchak on a Saturday or Sunday. No special December programme or holiday opening schedule was verified; allow flexibility around year-end.
uncertainties: Opening and closing times differ between tourism publications.
Current individual stall prices and accessible facilities remain unverified.
